question.problem: In winter, the maximum daily temperature of a certain mountain location (rounded to the nearest degree) varies between $-{15}^{∘}C$ and ${2}^{∘}C,$ inclusive. Assuming that for a given winter day, each maximum temperature value between $-{15}^{∘}C$ and ${2}^{∘}C$ has an equal probability of occurring, what is the probability that the maximum daily temperature will reach at least ${0}^{∘}C$ on a randomly selected day?
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the maximum daily temperature (rounded to the nearest degree Celsius). From the problem statement, we know that $X∼U\{-15,-14,…,2\},$ and we wish to compute $P(X\ge 0).$

In general, if $X$ follows a discrete uniform distribution over a set $S,$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{|S|}, & x\in S \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have $X∼U\{-15,-14,…,2\},$ and the set $S=\{-15,-14,…,2\}$ has $|S|=2-(-15)+1=18$ items. So, we have

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{18}, & x=-15,-14,…,2 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

In $S,$ the items that satisfy $X\ge 0$ are $0,1,2.$ There are $3$ of these elements. Therefore,

$$
P(X\ge 0)=3\cdot \frac{1}{18}=\frac{1}{6}.
$$
